expectations.text: Output identifies random negative sampling as a key validity problem (easy negatives inflate AUROC by 10-20pp)
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly flags uniform random negative sampling as inflating AUROC: 'If you are sampling negatives uniformly at random from all non-edges, many of those negatives are between nodes with no structural relationship whatsoever. This makes the task easier.' Also dedicates Option 3 and Option 4 to fixing negative sampling. Does not cite the specific 10-20pp figure, but clearly identifies it as a key validity problem.

expectations.text: Output specifically identifies GNN message-passing leakage: test edges are visible in the message-passing graph during node encoding, so the model effectively 'sees' the test answers while training
expectations.evidence: Response explains: 'The training graph includes edges that are neighbors of your test edges — nodes that appear in test edges still have their training-set connections visible. A GNN aggregates neighborhood features across multiple hops, so node embeddings learned during training are heavily shaped by the neighborhood structure that partially encodes the existence of test edges.' This clearly describes structural entanglement where the GNN encodes test-edge information through neighborhood aggregation, matching the core mechanism even without using the exact phrase 'adjacency matrix during message-passing.'

expectations.text: Output recommends a temporal train/test split (train on edges before time T, evaluate on edges after T) as the correct evaluation for the stated temporal forecasting goal
expectations.evidence: Option 1 is explicitly 'Temporal Split (Strongest Fix)' with: 'Training set: all edges with timestamp < T; Validation/test set: edges with timestamp >= T.' Also recommended in the detection section: 'Train on all edges formed before month T, evaluate on edges formed after month T.'

expectations.text: Output recommends comparing to a simple structural baseline (Adamic-Adar, Jaccard, or Common Neighbors) as a required sanity check
expectations.evidence: Detection step 1: 'Compare against structural heuristics. Compute Common Neighbors, Jaccard, and Adamic-Adar on the same 80/20 split and measure their AUROC.' Named explicitly as a sanity check.

expectations.text: Output recommends hard negative sampling (distance-2 non-edges or structurally similar non-edges) as a required fix
expectations.evidence: Option 3 explicitly states: 'Use hard negatives: sample negative pairs from nodes that are 2-hop neighbors but not directly connected, rather than uniform random non-edges.' This names distance-2 non-edges specifically.
